target_customer: Offices and office managers at tech companies, later HR, IT and facilities teams running hybrid workplaces
problem: Small and mid-size offices needed IT support and then general office management without a full-time hire, later desk and room management for hybrid work.
business_model: B2B SaaS and managed services, started as on-demand tech support

founders.name: Joe Du Bey
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked as an investor before Eden.

founders.name: Guy Morita
founders.background_notes: Listed as a former founder on the YC page only.

technical_complexity.rationale: At founding it was a services marketplace sending tech workers to customers. Software was a thin coordination layer.

defensibility.rationale: Service operations and vendor relationships were copyable. Managed by Q had a similar model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Eden bought rival Managed by Q from WeWork in March 2020 rather than being absorbed.

market_need_then: Growing startup offices lacked IT and facilities staff, and Eden moved from consumer home tech support to business customers within months of launching in 2015.

branding.domain_note: Now operates at edenworkplace.com, not the shorter eden.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Company describes itself as workplace software for people-centric companies

rebrands.why: Company blog post titled Eden is now Eden Workplace; year and reason not read

branding.community_and_virality: Acquired OrgOrg, a social network for office managers, in February 2018.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many companies. Press covered funding and deals, with no sourced evidence of brand-driven growth.

pivots.why: Moved to the enterprise space; fully by about three months later per search coverage
Expanded into supplies, cleaning and other office categories

outcome_analysis: Eden pivoted from consumer tech support to office management, raised a 10 million dollar Series A in September 2017 and a 25 million dollar Series B in November 2019, then bought rival Managed by Q in March 2020 and laid off about 40 percent of staff amid the pandemic. It still operates as Eden Workplace selling desk, room and visitor software. No acquisition of Eden itself was found despite the YC Acquired label.
notes: Directory status says Acquired but two searches found Eden only as an acquirer (OrgOrg 2018, Managed by Q 2020), so exit is recorded as unknown. The March 2020 JLL round amount (one snippet said 29M) was not verified, so null. Totals differ by source (38.3M Wellfound, 40M The Real Deal). Education was not found for any founder. Dated competitor search found only Managed by Q mentioned in the 2017 Series A article, which is not near the 2015 batch, so the founding-era list is empty. Eden Workplace is a different company from Eden Project.
